title: RegionSeal: Effect-Closed FPGA Regions at the Unchanged GGML Boundary
hook: Against the current strict backend's 11 accepted operator families and 112 graph signatures, RegionSeal adds exactly one recurring-region artifact and no new operator-family wrapper; it succeeds only if that artifact cuts matched pp512 or tg128 full-path median wall clock by at least 10% while retaining the same GGML admission, explicit-error, artifact-identity, and zero-fallback boundary.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: the strongest local baseline's breadth axis is its 11-family, 112-signature strict FPGA path, while the candidate is no broader on operator support and adds only one independently replaceable artifact. A surprising empirical reveal was also viable, but rejected because the direction of launch/wait reduction is expected; the defensible surprise is that one narrowly sealed region can test useful acceleration without whole-graph ownership or all-family vectorization.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf establishes that a framework-native backend can retain exact support decisions, explicit failure behavior, tensor-state continuity, and accelerator-artifact identity while execution no longer incurs one host-visible completion cycle per admitted unit — stakes: backend maintainers otherwise face either silent semantic drift and wrong outputs or a formally correct integration whose launch overhead blocks useful deployment and wastes FPGA development effort.
gap_closure.how_closed: C13 encodes the GGML tensor-effect connectivity as a verifiable region seal, and heterogeneous_decomposition uses that seal to substitute one pure effect-closed recurring region while mutable or externally aliased work stays on the strict per-node FPGA path; corpus support is thin in FPGA runtimes, with the closest C13 exemplars coming from relational-topology domains.

core_mechanism: RegionSeal first assigns every backend allocation a monotonic allocation_id and represents a tensor T by F(T) = {(allocation_id, [o + sum_k i_k nb_k, o + sum_k i_k nb_k + s_k)) for every valid logical index tuple i}, where o is the tensor's root-view byte offset, nb_k are GGML byte strides, and s_k is the stored byte width for the F16 element at that index; interval unions are normalized, bounds-checked, and derived from the complete GGML tensor metadata before launch. For every already-accepted node, a read/write effect is the pair of normalized footprint sets it may read and write, obtained from the operator implementation's explicit operand-role table rather than inferred from names. A candidate region is effect-closed only if every node is pure, every internal read is supplied by a region input or earlier region write, no write intersects any immutable input or tensor outside the region, and the region contains no KV update, in-place mutation, or externally visible state. It must have exactly one unaliased terminal output, that output must be graph-local and marked device-resident by the existing planner, and every downstream consumer must be an already-accepted strict FPGA node that reads it from one common XRT memory group. Among repeated contiguous DAG regions of length 2 through 6 in the complete pp512 and tg128 traces, the sole implemented region R* is selected by maximum baseline XRT wait time attributable to its occurrences, with ties broken by more occurrences and then lexicographic serialized GGML signature; thus no free region choice is left to the implementer. structural_prior_encoding produces the region seal: a digest over ordered node signatures, canonical effects, boundary tensor types/shapes/strides, the artifact kernel UUID, bounded loop limits, and a status schema, and a static checker certifies the stated disjointness and effect-closure conditions under the captured graph and allocation metadata. heterogeneous_decomposition consumes that seal by routing only exact R* matches to one finite HLS artifact and leaving every other accepted node, including all mutable or aliased state, on the existing strict per-node FPGA path rather than CPU fallback. The artifact executes synchronously into one fresh output BO allocated in the downstream consumers' common memory group, writes one status record, and has no externally outstanding dependent kernel. After one successful xrt::run wait and zero artifact status, the backend publishes that BO through the existing graph-local residency mirror path: ggml_fpga_residency_store installs one mirror keyed by the terminal GGML tensor, and later strict nodes resolve it through ggml_fpga_residency_get_input. This changes neither the GGML tensor nor its parent backend buffer. A completed nonzero status inserts no mirror and returns the existing explicit backend error. A timeout uses the existing run-abort failure path; if abort does not report a terminal state, the run and staging BO are quarantined and the backend is disabled for further work rather than resetting the device or claiming recoverable tensor continuity. Thus only successful execution publishes state, no CPU fallback is introduced, and a fault cannot expose a partial region output through the residency map. The novelty claim is the independently replaceable, digest-bound region contract and success-only single-output residency publication at the unchanged GGML backend boundary, not the ordinary fact that R*'s arithmetic is combined inside one artifact. For RegionSeal eligibility the footprint equation is restricted to F16 and its undefined s_k is the constant stored width 2, so F(T) is the checked union of [o + sum_k i_k nb_k, o + sum_k i_k nb_k + 2); block-quantized and other non-F16 accepted nodes remain on the existing strict path. Equivalent checked row-interval construction may replace per-element enumeration, and any offset, multiplication, end bound, or owning-allocation check that is unrepresentable or invalid makes the node ineligible for the region rather than producing a partial footprint. Effect closure additionally requires one region writer per byte, permits write-read overlap only from an earlier declared producer to its later consumers, and rejects overlap among terminal outputs or between a terminal output and any live outside tensor. The manifest alpha-renames process-local allocation_ids to canonical boundary and internal allocation slots, digests those slots and ranges, and requires the live seal check to establish a one-to-one slot-to-current-allocation binding before launch; raw process-local allocation_id values are not digest inputs.
core_mechanism_reasoning:
BLOCK 1 — PREMISES ledger:
P1. GGML views and backend tensors expose sufficient root allocation, offset, shape, stride, and type metadata to derive exact F16 byte footprints; the current backend already resolves these fields to launch accepted operators.
P2. Pure recurring regions exist in both llama-bench pp512 and tg128 traces — untested — falsification target; recurrence and attributable wait mass must be established from the supplied complete traces before R* is built.
P3. A strict node outside R* can consume a successfully published residency mirror without changing its support decision; the current backend already stores graph-local mirrors by tensor and retrieves them for same-group downstream consumers, while support remains keyed by operator/type/shape.
P4. A finite single artifact plus one synchronous wait has no unresolved cross-kernel dependency after successful return; all loop bounds are sealed, completed nonzero status is propagated before publication, and an unconfirmed timeout abort disables the backend while retaining the run/BO lifetime instead of promising recovery.
observation-model: the 2,422 accepted U280 dispatch observations and pp512/tg128 traces are complete for the measured Gemma 3 1B F16 llama-bench runs because hooks record every accepted GGML call, XRT start, and wait, but they are not an unbiased sample of other models or prompts, so claims remain scoped to this path.
ESTIMAND: for each fixed llama-bench regime pp512 and tg128 on the baseline Gemma 3 1B F16 GGUF and one U280, the target is the paired median end-to-end wall-clock time across 30 post-warmup runs, together with the fraction of baseline XRT wait time and starts attributable to exact R* occurrences.
BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT: The naive runnable version detects a repeated GGML node sequence, replaces it with one fused XRT kernel, and writes directly to the original destination BO. Branch (i): it falsely assumes node sequence, shape, and tensor name determine non-aliasing and that a failed launch may safely have touched the destination; legal GGML views can overlap one canonical allocation, so RegionSeal confronts this with exact allocation-range effects, exclusion of external aliases, a single fresh output BO, and success-only publication into the backend's existing graph-residency mirror map. Alias/effect analysis is a standard compiler tool, but this instance is not solved by that tool alone because an unchanged GGML backend neither owns graph rewriting nor may change per-node admission, explicit no-fallback behavior, XRT artifact identity, or tensor-storage lifetime; the seal binds those runtime-specific obligations to an independently replaceable artifact.
BLOCK 3 — The anchor is one gap with a chain, so the same seal is deliberately the intermediate object: structural encoding constructs it and heterogeneous decomposition consumes it; no auxiliary module is added. Ordinary fusion, command capture, a persistent overlay, compiler-owned dataflow, asynchronous version polling, and MVCC/COW epochs were rejected because they land on occupied lineage nodes or recreate progress and alias hazards; direct writes were rejected because failure could expose partial storage, tensor/backend-buffer rebinding was rejected because GGML tensors are offsets in shared buffers, and all-11 wrappers were rejected because one R* is sufficient for the minimal wall-clock test. Implementation grounding is the clean fpga-backend source at commit 2616bb6b0fabfe2974c00bf3a2d5be292a22e05e: ggml-fpga-xrt.cpp already defines ggml_fpga_residency_state::mirrors plus ggml_fpga_residency_store/get_input and ggml_fpga_wait_for_run, so the candidate extends an executable publication/failure path rather than inventing a GGML tensor-rebinding API.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Add allocation_id and root-view tracking to the existing GGML FPGA tensor metadata; input GGML tensor descriptors produce normalized, overflow-checked F16 footprint interval sets keyed by the owning XRT BO.
2. Add explicit read/write operand-role tables for the currently accepted implementations and run the effect extractor before graph launch; input nodes and canonical footprints produce per-node effects plus overlap edges.
3. Scan the existing complete Gemma 3 1B F16 pp512/tg128 traces for repeated contiguous DAG regions of two to six pure accepted nodes, reject any region with KV mutation, in-place writes, external aliases, or non-closed effects, and deterministically emit R* using the wait-mass selection rule.
4. Serialize R* into a region-seal manifest containing node signatures, boundary metadata, normalized effects, bounded dimensions, status codes, and artifact UUID; the manifest checker either emits a digest-qualified substitution entry or leaves every node on the current strict FPGA path.
5. Implement and synthesize exactly one U280 HLS artifact for R*, reusing the current arithmetic kernels where practical but writing its sole terminal result to one fresh BO in the required consumer memory group plus a status record; its output is one xclbin kernel whose bounded control returns only after all R* arithmetic completes.
6. At the unchanged GGML graph-compute boundary, rerun the seal check against live allocation_ids and ranges, start the digest-matched artifact once, and synchronously wait once; a mismatch executes the same accepted nodes through the current strict per-node FPGA path, never CPU fallback.
7. On successful XRT wait and zero artifact status, insert the one fresh output BO into the existing graph-residency mirror map for R*'s terminal tensor; downstream same-group strict nodes consume it through the existing residency lookup, without rebinding a GGML tensor or backend buffer. On completed failure, insert nothing and return the existing explicit error. On unconfirmed timeout abort, quarantine the run and BO and disable the backend for subsequent work; do not reset the device or claim request recovery.
8. Add regression tests with overlapping offset/strided views, allocation reuse, forced digest mismatch, injected nonzero artifact status, XRT timeout, and downstream same-group consumers; outputs are compared with the unchanged CPU path and current strict FPGA path, and every negative case must produce no residency publication, an explicit error when applicable, and no CPU fallback.
9. Before synthesis, compute W_R for pp512 and tg128 and terminate the candidate if no eligible R* covers at least 20% of baseline end-to-end time in either regime. Otherwise run llama-bench pp512 and tg128 on the existing Gemma 3 1B F16 GGUF for 30 paired post-warmup repetitions per arm, recording end-to-end wall clock, GGML calls, XRT starts/waits, outputs, tokens, status traces, residency publications, and artifact UUIDs for strict baseline, RegionSeal, and manifest-disabled control. For Step 2, a node is region-eligible only when its implementation variant has a complete physical read/write entry covering conditional operands, padding, vector over-read or over-write, and implementation-visible scratch; an absent or incomplete entry leaves that node on the current strict path. For Step 3, a region is a consecutive interval in captured trace order, recurrence means at least two exact signature occurrences in the combined pp512 and tg128 trace corpus, and each signature is scored by summed integer wait duration over its deterministic maximum-weight pairwise non-overlapping occurrence set, with ties broken by occurrence count, serialized signature, and lexicographic occurrence-index list in that order. If Step 3 finds no eligible repeated region, it records P2 as failed and terminates RegionSeal candidate construction before manifest generation or synthesis, with the existing strict backend left unchanged.
falsification_prediction: Use the existing complete U280 traces as a zero-build gate: if no deterministic effect-closed R* exists or its sealed wait coverage W_R is below 0.20 of baseline end-to-end time in both pp512 and tg128, reject the idea before synthesis. If the gate passes, run unchanged llama.cpp and Gemma 3 1B F16 on the same Alveo U280 for 30 paired post-warmup trials under the current strict backend, RegionSeal, and a manifest-disabled control. Success requires exact R* occurrences to collapse to one start and one wait, zero CPU fallback, matched output/token checks, and at least a 10% reduction in median full-path wall clock in one regime with a paired-bootstrap 95% confidence interval excluding zero; otherwise the performance claim is falsified. The load-bearing variable is W_R, and disabling only the seal match must return wall clock toward the strict baseline. Any residency publication after nonzero status, any changed aliased byte, any absent explicit error, any artifact-digest mismatch that still launches R*, or any downstream consumer that reads a different BO than the published mirror falsifies the contract. A timeout need only produce explicit failure, no publication, and backend disablement; recoverable continuation after device failure is outside the claim.
compute_budget: 0 GPU-day + $0 API; approximately 14-18 engineer-weeks, one U280, 40-80 Vitis synthesis/place-and-route runs, and about 200 board-hours, feasible within five months.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: Its selector replays measured per-operator and directed transition costs without an integrated runtime, whereas RegionSeal constructs and executes a live digest-bound GGML region with canonical BO-range effects, one synchronous completion, and success-only publication through the existing same-group residency mirror path.

Its host agent may choose CPU execution and retrieves FPGA output before subsequent layer progress, whereas RegionSeal preserves zero fallback and substitutes only a statically effect-closed pure region while every excluded node remains on the existing strict FPGA path.

ATLAS generates whole-model hardware through a universal GEMM abstraction, whereas RegionSeal constructs a single independently replaceable artifact contract over native GGML signatures, canonical view ranges, failure status, and atomic BO publication at the unchanged backend boundary (abstract-only inference because its full text is unavailable in the supplied cache).

what_step_was_missed: ATLAS would have needed to derive canonical GGML allocation-range effects and bind them, explicit failure status, artifact identity, and success-only publication into a framework-native residency mirror to form a per-region contract that remains valid without owning or rewriting the application graph.
